subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The little book of Mao's sayings carried by the Red Guards was known by what colour?
questions.explain: Mao's quotations were published as the 'Little Red Book'.

questions.q: Who led the Nationalists (GMD) against the Communists in the Chinese Civil War?
questions.explain: Chiang Kai-shek led the Nationalist GMD against Mao's Communists.

questions.q: Roughly how many people are estimated to have died in the famine caused by the Great Leap Forward?
questions.explain: The famine of around 1959-1962 killed tens of millions, making it one of history's worst.

questions.q: In which year did Mao Zedong proclaim the founding of the People's Republic of China?
questions.explain: Mao proclaimed the People's Republic of China on 1 October 1949.

questions.q: Which 1972 visit marked a thaw between Communist China and the USA?
questions.explain: US President Nixon visited China in 1972, easing Cold War tensions.

questions.q: The Communists' epic 1934-35 retreat from Nationalist forces is known as what?
questions.explain: The Long March (1934-35) saved the Communists and confirmed Mao's leadership.

questions.q: In which years did the Chinese Civil War resume in full after the defeat of Japan, ending in Communist victory?
questions.explain: After Japan's 1945 defeat, the renewed civil war ran from 1946 to the Communist victory in 1949.

questions.q: Mao's 1958 campaign of rapid industrialisation and communes was called what?
questions.explain: The Great Leap Forward (1958) led to economic chaos and a massive famine.

questions.q: In 1989 pro-democracy protests were crushed by the army in which Beijing location?
questions.explain: The Tiananmen Square protests were violently suppressed in June 1989.

questions.q: After Mao's death, which leader introduced market-style economic reforms from the late 1970s?
questions.explain: Deng Xiaoping opened China's economy with his reform programme.

questions.q: Backyard furnaces during the Great Leap Forward were meant to boost production of what?
questions.explain: Peasants built backyard furnaces to make steel, but the metal was largely useless.

questions.q: After losing the civil war in 1949, Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists retreated to which island?
questions.explain: The defeated Nationalists fled to Taiwan in 1949 after the Communist victory.

questions.q: In which year did the Korean War begin, drawing in Mao's new People's Republic?
questions.explain: China entered the Korean War, which began in 1950, against UN forces.

questions.q: Which 1937 conflict saw Japan invade China, forcing Communists and Nationalists into an uneasy alliance?
questions.explain: Japan's full invasion of China in 1937 began the Second Sino-Japanese War.

questions.q: The group blamed for Cultural Revolution excesses and arrested after Mao's death was called what?
questions.explain: The Gang of Four, including Mao's wife Jiang Qing, were arrested in 1976.

questions.q: The famine following the Great Leap Forward killed millions chiefly during which years?
questions.explain: The Great Leap famine caused tens of millions of deaths roughly between 1959 and 1962.

questions.q: In which year did Mao Zedong die, opening a power struggle in China?
questions.explain: Mao Zedong died in 1976.

questions.q: What was the early Communist policy of taking land from landlords and giving it to peasants called?
questions.explain: Land reform from 1950 redistributed land and often killed landlords.

questions.q: Which close ally of Mao, named as his successor, died in a 1971 plane crash after an alleged coup plot?
questions.explain: Lin Biao, Mao's designated heir, died in a 1971 plane crash fleeing China after a reputed plot.

questions.q: Deng Xiaoping's modernisation programme from the late 1970s was summarised as the 'Four' what?
questions.explain: Deng promoted the 'Four Modernisations' of agriculture, industry, defence and science from 1978.

questions.q: The 'Four Olds' attacked during the Cultural Revolution included old customs, culture, habits and what?
questions.explain: The Red Guards attacked the 'Four Olds': old ideas, culture, customs and habits.

questions.q: Who succeeded Mao as Communist Party leader immediately after his death in 1976, before being sidelined by Deng?
questions.explain: Hua Guofeng briefly led China after Mao's 1976 death before Deng Xiaoping gained dominance.
